note:
Paper 91, Team 44398, the bathtub heat-transfer paper. Fifty-one pages, sixty-four measured
regions over twenty-seven of them, and the sixty-four resolve into THIRTY-SIX figure rows, TWELVE
tables and SIXTEEN exclusions. Unaccounted zero. Six printed tables are declared gaps with no
measured region at all - Tables 2 and 3 on p14, Tables 4 and 5 on p23, Table 6 on p29 and Table 16 on
p44 - and pp14 and p23 carry no region whatsoever even though the region pass reported 32 vector
paths on each, so the twelve counted tables are the twelve the pass actually boxed and the eighteen
printed tables are the paper's real count.

The sixteen exclusions are all fragments or furniture, never exhibits. Nine are keys and colour bars
that the pass boxes as their own regions - the legends of Figures 6, 10 and 12, the colour bars of
Figures 7, 11, 13 and 24 - and four more are the lettering strips of Figures 3 and 4 ('Layers of
thermal insulation materials', 'Inside the tub', 'Outside the tub', 'ft ft2'). One is the display
strip of inequality (45) on p34, one is a block of the summary sheet's body text on p49, and one is a
second slice of p49's banner. That banner, a magenta 'Why' and a footprint glyph on p49 are recorded as
exhibits with captions of 'none', because the region pass boxes them and they are figure-sized
graphics, though the honest reading is that they are typographic furniture of the paper's two-column
summary sheet - the only three rows here at medium confidence.

Seven exhibits are multi-panel and sixteen of the thirty-six rows are their panels: Figure 7 is two
temperature fields on pp17 sharing one unlabelled colour bar, Figure 11 is five snapshots at 1, 2, 10,
20 and 30 seconds split across pp24-25, Figure 13 is two snapshots at 3 and 15 seconds, and Figure 24
is the four entrance arrangements in a 2x2 block. None of the sixteen prints an axis, a graduation or a
value; the panels are comparable only because they are printed at one size and share a bar, and the
paper's conclusions about evenness are judgements of colour uniformity.

CAPTIONS. Every caption is a label plus a noun phrase, one line, no unit, no source, no condition; all
thirty-three printed figure captions sit below their picture and all twelve table captions above their
grid. The text layer cannot render the subscripts, so seven figure captions come out as glyph runs
('The change of q \uf046 and 2 T over volume') and those seven are typed from the crops. Two caption
defects are worth naming: Table 15's caption omits the parameter it varies - it reads only 'The
variation of parameters' and h3 survives only as a column head, so Tables 14 and 15 are
indistinguishable from their captions - and Figure 21 keeps a space after the period ('Fig. 21') where
every other label in the paper closes it up, and Table 7 drops the space ('Table7').

CITATION. This is the thinnest citation in the lane so far. Eleven figure rows and eleven of the twelve
counted tables are named by no sentence at all; the introduction to an exhibit is a bare 'as follows',
'as follows' being the paper's standard transition, printed immediately before the caption. Only
twenty-five figure rows carry a pointer and most of those are one of three fixed phrases - 'the above
figure', 'the following figure', 'the above picture' - with no reading of the drawing in them. Two
pointers are worse than none: p16 prints 'The curve of residual is shown in Fig.5' for the figure its
own caption numbers Fig.6, so Figure 6 has no correct pointer anywhere in fifty-one pages, and p45's
introduction to Table 18 is truncated mid-clause ('From point of'), leaving the table named only by
its caption. Figure 2 is the one exhibit named a page after it prints, and Figure 10 the other.

WHAT THE PICTURES SHOW. Figure 6 is the Fluent residual plot and it is the most informative single
image in the paper: six residuals on a log axis to iteration 400, key box inside the plot at the upper
right, NEITHER AXIS TITLED, no tolerance line anywhere - and at the 379 iterations where the prose
declares the problem 'nearly convergent' five of the six residuals are still between 1e-03 and 1e-04,
which is not a convergence at any standard tolerance. Figure 9 draws three temperature trends on two
axes that are bare arrows with symbol ticks, so it prints no numbers and cannot be read for a value at
all. Figures 15 to 22 are eight dual-ordinate plots: each pairs two variables of different units on
left and right scales, keys inside, and in each pair the two lines are read as one story although the
scales are unrelated - Figure 20 is the clearest case, where one 'proportional' series is dead flat at
the top of its axis and the other moves across a window of 0.00035 kg/s. Figures 21 and 22 print 'The
change of h3/(W/(m2K))' over ticks reading 50 to 70, so the axis label and its numbers disagree about
whether the abscissa is a percentage or a coefficient. Figure 17 labels its right ordinate 'the change
of T2 /mi', a wreck of the degree sign, and puts five unordered tub shapes on a categorical axis.
Figure 5 is a Gambit screenshot whose grid aliases at print size. Figures 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 18 and 23 are

rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: sixty-four measured regions resolve into thirty-six figure rows, twelve tables and sixteen exclusions, and no region is counted twice [place.page_order].

A panel measured as its own box is its own row: the four multi-panel exhibits of this paper (Figures 7, 11, 13, 24) are split into two, five, two and four measured boxes, so the figure count follows the boxes and the panel_count names the exhibit they belong to [geometry.panel_count].

A key or colour bar that the region pass boxes on its own is an exclusion, not a figure: the legends of Figures 6, 10 and 12 and the colour bars of Figures 7, 11, 13 and 24 are fragments of the exhibits they serve [place.area_frac].

A label or lettering strip drawn inside a diagram and boxed separately is a fragment of that diagram: the four 'Layers of thermal insulation materials / Inside the tub / Outside the tub / ft ft2' strips of pp12 belong to Figures 3 and 4 [place.area_frac].
A display equation boxed as a vector block is not an exhibit: p34 r4 holds inequality (45) and carries no data, so it is excluded rather than counted as a table or figure [place.section_kind].
A strip of body text boxed as a region is not an exhibit: p49 r4 holds two columns of prose from the summary sheet [place.section_kind].
A graphic sliced twice on one page is counted once: p49's banner is measured as a full raster and as an overlapping slice, and the second is a duplicate of the first [place.page_order].

A caption transcribed off the crop is typed-from-crop when the text layer cannot produce it: seven captions print their subscripts as glyph runs (phi_q and T2 come out of the text layer as 'q \uf046' and '2 T'), so those seven are read off the pixels [caption.verbatim].

A caption that the text layer prints intact is text-layer and is quoted from it, including the missing space in 'Table7' and the space in 'Fig. 21', which are what the page prints [caption.numbering].
A caption naming its variables in symbols counts them: the T2/phi_q and qm1/qm2 captions all carry two variables, the rest carry none [caption.variables].
Every printed caption in this paper sits BELOW its figure and ABOVE its table, without exception, so position is read off the block order and not guessed [caption.position].

A pointer that names 'the above figure', 'the following figure' or 'the above picture' is as-shown-in and its count is one per figure even when the same sentence serves a pair of panels [mention.lead_pattern].

An exhibit that no sentence names is recorded with first_page None and count 0 rather than attributed the nearest 'as follows': eleven figure rows and eleven of the twelve counted tables are in that state [mention.count].
An exhibit named after it prints takes a negative lead_pages: Figure 2 prints on p9 and is first named on p10, and Figure 10 prints on p24 and is first named on p25 [mention.lead_pages].

A pointer that prints the wrong number is recorded against the number it prints: p16 says 'The curve of residual is shown in Fig.5' for the figure captioned Fig.6, so the pointer counts under Figure 5 and Figure 6 stays uncited [mention.lead_sentence].
A colour-mapped field with no axis, no graduation and no numbers is heatmap-or-contour even when its colour bar is a separate region, and printed_numbers stays false [geometry.printed_numbers].
A figure whose marks are joined by drawn strokes is line even when each stroke is short and straight between two categories, as Figure 17's five-tub comparison is [geometry.family].
A dual-ordinate plot is line and takes legend inside when the key box is drawn within the plot area, which is Figures 14 to 22 [geometry.legend].
A schematic, sketch or flow chart with no numeric axis is flowchart-or-schematic: Figures 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 18 and 23 all draw structure rather than data [geometry.family].
A screenshot of a mesh viewport is photo-or-raster-image and not a schematic: Figure 5 is a screen export whose grid aliases at print size [geometry.family].
A banner, pull-quote word or decorative glyph has no vocabulary class and takes other with an other_note naming what the lettering says [geometry.family].
A table caption that omits its parameter is recorded as printed, not reconstructed: Table 15 reads 'The variation of parameters' and h3 survives only as a column head [caption.verbatim].
A closed box with vertical strokes between columns is boxed, and a grid with a rule above the header only is booktabs - ten of the twelve counted tables take booktabs [table.rule_style].
A merged band header is recorded with the header row count it needs: Tables 12, 17 and 18 all carry merged cells, Table 17 carries two header levels [table.header_rows].
A table whose cells each carry their own percent sign is decimal_aligned when the signs form a colon, which Tables 14 and 15 do and Table 13 does not [table.decimal_aligned].
A footnote under a grid is recorded as the table's note_sentence only when it is a printed sentence: Tables 11 and 18 both carry one, Table 8's sketches carry none [table.note_sentence].
Six printed tables have NO measured region and are declared gaps rather than invented rows: Tables 2 and 3 on p14, Tables 4 and 5 on p23, Table 6 on p29 and Table 16 on p44 [table.rows].

tables.note: The symbol table: fourteen symbols (h, k, cp, rho, delta, t, tau, qm, Phi, T, V, M/m, A, a/b/c) against their definitions and units, three columns and a single header row. Two rows pack several symbols into one cell ('M, m' and 'a, b, c') and the unit column carries alternatives ('W / (m2 K)', 'kg / m2', 's, min, h', 'm, L'), so a lookup of one symbol sometimes lands on a cell that defines two. Units are in the header only for the column; the cells carry their own. No rule between data rows.

caption.verbatim: Table7 Variation of some parameters

tables.note: Seven columns (V, A1, A2, T2, qm1, qm2, phi_q) by eleven variation rows from -15.00% to +15.00% in steps that skip 10%, so the sweep the prose describes (+-5, 8, 12, 15) is printed as eleven levels including zero. EVERY CELL CARRIES ITS OWN PERCENT SIGN, so there is no unit column and no units row, and the 0.00% row in the middle is the baseline. The left column is the swept volume change, the other six are responses; the sign pattern (A2 and phi_q fall fastest at -15%, qm1 hardly moves) is the table's message. The caption prints 'Table7' with no space.

caption.verbatim: Table 12 The heat transfer coefficients

tables.note: Four columns with TWO MERGED VERTICAL BANDS: 'Natural convection' and 'Forced convection' now span three rows each, and the W/(m2K) unit cell is merged down the same five rows, so the grid reads as two blocks separated by a mid-table rule. Above each block a pair of unruled rows gives the coefficients of air and water ('Coefficient of air 1~10', 'Coefficient of water 200~1000'), which are ranges rather than the single values the model uses - the table states both the range it drew from and the value it picked without saying which is which.

tables.note: Identical skeleton to Table 14 with h3 as the swept column head - five columns, eleven variation rows, percent signs forming a colon, decimals aligned.
